findings: A live proof found two defects that six increments of fixture-tested work could not, in ninety seconds and for nothing. Both were the same shape: a fixture builds its request the way the contract says to, so no fixture could see that a route, or the contract itself, disagreed with what the service would accept.

The second defect is the more instructive: a capability file states what the adapter will ask for, and it asked for a format sold with a plan above the operator's. That is unobservable without asking the service, which is exactly what a live proof does.

A failed take holds the vendor's budget line just as a successful one does. Four failures from attempt 2 hold $2.22 of the $25 line with nothing to show for it, and only an operator invoice allocation clears them. A vendor line will therefore drift toward its alerts on failures alone.
knownGaps: ElevenLabs holds do not settle on their own, exactly as the Azure ones do not. They clear when the operator allocates the vendor's invoice.
The premade catalogue has no old female voice, so an elderly woman is cast middle-aged. The account, not the studio, decides what is available.
The titled picture edit took 238 s for a 14 s film, on the known editorial render path.
